rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

All pronouns and demonstratives resolve in the current chunk or earlier named deck context.

The cross-file pointers name their documents directly: chunk 2, expanded line 9 (raw line 9), "The Missing Check"; chunk 8, expanded line 72 (raw line 60), "What is an Agent, The autonomy ladder". No callback identifies a source by opening or page position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: N/A: the expanded body contains no backward-beat form such as "the X you did/saw/caught" that requires resolution against a current exercise or lecture beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: N/A: no guess, predict, or guess-before-reveal instruction appears in the expanded body; the only prompt fence is exempt and contains no such demo beat either.

Every body chunk carries a self-carrying claim, instruction, artifact handoff, or next action. For example, chunk 6, expanded line 60 (raw line 48), explains why boundary control and read-back verification matter; no chunk is only a wait-state or context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 9 "Key Concepts": expanded line 76 (raw line 64), "## Key Concepts", is followed by six consolidation claims; the heading accurately describes the projected content. The other module headings likewise match their claims, instructions, or logistics.

Checked all six sub-items across the expanded body. The closest contrast is chunk 4, expanded line 25 (raw line 25), "This module is the rescue. Not full closure:" — a single contrast, not a Not-X/Not-Y/Z triple; chunk 8's "Propose, double-check, apply" (expanded line 70, raw line 58) has three concrete verbs. No empty anaphora triple, self-grading superlative, number retraction, abstraction-noun stack, or empty verb triplet appears.
